question: Should Testbox lease freshness guarantee that its caller returns after 120 seconds even when Git is stuck in uninterruptible filesystem I/O, or is a best-effort timeout for signal-responsive Git processes the intended contract?
rationale: The answer determines whether this needs a supervising process/non-blocking execution model or only narrower wording and evidence; the PR cannot safely choose that operational contract on its own.

options.title: Require a hard caller deadline
options.body: Use a supervisor or other execution model that can report lease freshness failure without waiting for a blocked Git worker to close, and add focused proof for that behavior.

options.title: Accept best-effort child termination
options.body: Keep the synchronous timeout but narrow the user-facing claim and proof to signal-responsive Git hangs rather than stale or unresponsive filesystem I/O.

recommendation.title: Require a hard caller deadline
recommendation.body: Use a supervisor or other execution model that can report lease freshness failure without waiting for a blocked Git worker to close, and add focused proof for that behavior.
